clippings.speaker: Robert Rodriguez
clippings.quote: So I'd go show him storyboards from Desperado, he'd come act out scenes of Pulp Fiction. And we got to be really good friends that way.
clippings.title: Transcript for Robert Rodriguez: Sin City, Desperado, El Mariachi, Alita, and Filmmaking
clippings.context: Podcast #465 interview; Rodriguez recalls their neighboring offices on the Sony lot while he wrote Desperado and Tarantino wrote Pulp Fiction.

clippings.speaker: Robert Rodriguez
clippings.quote: Quentin loved the characters of the brothers so much, he spent half the script with them before even getting to the bar.
clippings.title: Robert Rodriguez reveals Samuel L. Jackson's 'Pulp Fiction' speech was almost Harvey Keitel's in 'From Dusk Till Dawn'
clippings.context: Said by Rodriguez, as reported by Gold Derby, about the From Dusk Till Dawn script Tarantino wrote; the quote is from a 30th-anniversary screening at the Academy Museum.

clippings.speaker: Robert Rodriguez
clippings.quote: But when I realized that if I shot his movie, it would start looking too much like one of mine and he's wanted to be his own D.P. for a while.
clippings.title: Interview With Grindhouse Directors Quentin Tarantino And Robert Rodriguez
clippings.context: Joint Grindhouse interview; Rodriguez explains why he did not shoot Tarantino's film himself.

clippings.speaker: Quentin Tarantino
clippings.quote: Robert's movie is so similar in style and feel to a John Carpenter movie, we've always been joking that, it's like the zombie movie John Carpenter should've made in between Escape from New York and The Thing.
clippings.title: An interview with Quentin Tarantino
clippings.context: Grindhouse-era interview by Sebastian Haselbeck; the page is undated, so the year is inferred from the Grindhouse release.

clippings.speaker: Quentin Tarantino
clippings.quote: In almost every category of the two films working together, we didn't want any sameness going on. If mine had been distressed in the exact same way that Robert's had been distressed it would look like we just pushed a button.
clippings.title: Interview With Grindhouse Directors Quentin Tarantino And Robert Rodriguez
clippings.context: Joint Grindhouse interview; Tarantino explains why the two films were given different looks.

clippings.speaker: Quentin Tarantino
clippings.quote: With 'Grindhouse,' I think me and Robert just felt that people had a little more of a concept of the history of double features and exploitation movies... No, they didn't. At all.
clippings.title: Tarantino Misjudged Viewers' 'Grindhouse' Interest: 'It Meant Nothing to Them'
clippings.context: Tarantino on the film's US reception, quoted by IndieWire from an Empire magazine Q&A.

notes: Tarantino-side quotes are thinner; the MovieWeb Sin City panel and Texas Monthly were unreachable. The Tarantino archive interview is undated (year inferred).
